Forecast Discussion

NWS Detroit/Pontiac · 1258 PM EST Mon Nov 23 2026
 

- Scattered rain/snow showers this afternoon transition to mainly
  snow this evening. Pockets of brief, intense snowfall will be
  possible north of a line from Owosso to Mt. Clemens.

- Widespread rain on Thursday and Friday with rain/snow mix possible
  Thursday night and Friday night.

&&

.AVIATION...

Surface pressure gradually rises through the TAF period as high 
pressure builds in from the Plains. This has led to a moderate 
gradient across the Great Lakes, with sustained WNW flow of 10-15 
knots. Wind direction focused across Lake Superior and Lake Michigan 
has led to a healthy plume of 3-5 kft based stratocumulus that is 
expanding southeast at issuance. Meanwhile, a strong upper level 
disturbance is approaching the Great Lakes and will increase 
precipitation production through the afternoon. This means an 
increase in lake enhanced rain-snow potential late this afternoon, 
transitioning to all snow as temperatures drop with sunset. The wave 
will be strongest over the Tri Cities and Thumb where a quick burst 
of snow will be possible between roughly 21z-03z. Rain-snow showers 
may survive further south, but lose intensity away from their lake 
moisture source to inhibit long duration/widespread vsby 
restrictions. Minor accumulations on grassy/elevated surfaces remain 
possible.  

For DTW...Potential  for ceilings to drop below 5000 feet increases 
this afternoon-evening as lake moisture expands into SE Michigan. A 
strong upper level disturbance then supports a chance for light lake 
effect rain and snow showers to clip DTW, although the heavier 
precipitation is expected to stay north of the terminal. 

.DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES...

* Low in ceilings aob 5000 feet this afternoon, then medium this 
  evening and low overnight.

* Medium confidence in precip type being melting snow this evening.
